variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Production LangChain is the practice of operating a LangChain application as a reliable software system, not merely getting a model call to work. LangChain supplies model, tool, agent, and middleware abstractions; LangGraph supplies lower-level stateful orchestration; LangSmith can supply tracing, evaluation, and deployment services.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: LangChain
pairs.detail: Integrates models and tools and provides create_agent, middleware, structured output, streaming, and runnable composition.
pairs.explanation: Integrates models and tools and provides create_agent, middleware, structured output, streaming, and runnable composition. Use it when the supplied abstraction matches the control loop you need.

pairs.label: LangGraph
pairs.detail: Models explicit state and transitions for long-running or custom workflows.
pairs.explanation: Models explicit state and transitions for long-running or custom workflows. Checkpointers can persist thread state so a run can pause, resume, and recover from the last recorded step.

pairs.label: LangSmith
pairs.detail: Records nested traces, supports offline and online evaluation, and offers managed or self-hosted deployment options.
pairs.explanation: Records nested traces, supports offline and online evaluation, and offers managed or self-hosted deployment options. It is useful infrastructure, not a substitute for application policy.

variants.hint:
LangChain: Integrates models and tools and provides create_agent, middleware, structured output, streaming, and runnable composition.

LangGraph: Models explicit state and transitions for long-running or custom workflows.

LangSmith: Records nested traces, supports offline and online evaluation, and offers managed or self-hosted deployment options.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Deterministic pipeline
pairs.detail: Use typed stages when the order and allowed operations are known before execution.
pairs.explanation: Use typed stages when the order and allowed operations are known before execution. This is easiest to test, budget, cache, and explain.

pairs.label: LangChain agent
pairs.detail: Use an agent when the model must select among approved tools or decide how many loop iterations are needed.
pairs.explanation: Use an agent when the model must select among approved tools or decide how many loop iterations are needed. Keep tool authority, iteration count, and stop conditions explicit.

pairs.label: Custom LangGraph
pairs.detail: Use a graph when the application needs explicit branches, parallel work, checkpoints, approval pauses, or recovery that must resume at a known boundary.
pairs.explanation: Use a graph when the application needs explicit branches, parallel work, checkpoints, approval pauses, or recovery that must resume at a known boundary.

pairs.label: Admit a run
pairs.detail: Authenticate the caller, authorize the use case, assign a run and thread identity, and attach an idempotency key for any business operation.
pairs.explanation: Authenticate the caller, authorize the use case, assign a run and thread identity, and attach an idempotency key for any business operation.

pairs.label: Bind the budget
pairs.detail: Set an absolute deadline, model and tool limits, maximum loop count, cancellation signal, and spend envelope before orchestration begins.
pairs.explanation: Set an absolute deadline, model and tool limits, maximum loop count, cancellation signal, and spend envelope before orchestration begins.

pairs.label: Execute typed stages
pairs.detail: Validate state transitions and tool arguments.
pairs.explanation: Validate state transitions and tool arguments. Keep credentials and policy outside prompts, and checkpoint only state that can be serialized and safely resumed.

pairs.label: Commit an outcome
pairs.detail: Return a validated result, a truthful pending state, or a classified failure.
pairs.explanation: Return a validated result, a truthful pending state, or a classified failure. Record release, trace, cost, and side-effect identifiers for diagnosis.

pairs.label: Run context
pairs.detail: Carries request-scoped identity, credentials, feature flags, deadlines, and cancellation.
pairs.explanation: Carries request-scoped identity, credentials, feature flags, deadlines, and cancellation. Do not persist secrets into prompts or checkpoints merely because tools need them.

pairs.label: Checkpointer
pairs.detail: Stores graph snapshots and pending writes for conversation continuity, human review, time travel, and fault recovery.
pairs.explanation: Stores graph snapshots and pending writes for conversation continuity, human review, time travel, and fault recovery. A stable thread_id selects the state to resume.

pairs.label: Store
pairs.detail: Holds application-defined long-term information such as preferences or facts.
pairs.explanation: Holds application-defined long-term information such as preferences or facts. It needs tenant isolation, retention, deletion, and provenance rules.

pairs.label: System of record
pairs.detail: Owns payments, orders, tickets, or other effects.
pairs.explanation: Owns payments, orders, tickets, or other effects. A checkpoint may record an operation ID, but it must not replace reconciliation with the authoritative service.

pairs.label: Application service
pairs.detail: Run a fixed chain or short agent behind your existing API service when normal request timeouts, stateless replicas, and external persistence cover the workload.
pairs.explanation: Run a fixed chain or short agent behind your existing API service when normal request timeouts, stateless replicas, and external persistence cover the workload.

pairs.label: Standalone Agent Server
pairs.detail: Package graphs with the Agent Server runtime and operate its PostgreSQL, Redis, workers, upgrades, and capacity.
pairs.explanation: Package graphs with the Agent Server runtime and operate its PostgreSQL, Redis, workers, upgrades, and capacity. Avoid scale-to-zero for queued long-running work.

pairs.label: Managed or self-hosted platform
pairs.detail: Use LangSmith Deployment when its threads, runs, persistence, task queue, streaming, and horizontal-scaling model fit your operational requirements and governance.
